name: Juniper
waitingLines: I’m fine. Just chilling on your couch till {partner} shows up. Don’t mind me.
Not leaving till I’ve said hi to {partner}. Also your snacks are good. Mostly that.

questions.scene: Juniper strolls in wearing sunglasses indoors, holding a family-size bag of chips.
lines: I'm fine. Totally fine. Anyway, I brought trivia. And these chips are mine.
questions.question: When a red fox pounces on prey under snow, what helps it aim?

choices.label: Smelling the snow's vibes
reply: Vibes are real, but no.
Scientists think foxes use Earth's magnetic field to aim their pounce.
They land better facing northeast. Nature's cheat code.

choices.label: Closing their eyes and hoping
reply: That's literally how I date. Didn't work either.
Foxes likely use Earth's magnetic field to aim pounces.
Northeast-facing jumps hit way more often. Wild, right?

choices.label: Earth's magnetic field
reply: Okay, you're smart. Annoyingly smart.
Red foxes pounce more accurately facing roughly northeast, likely using Earth's magnetism.
Built-in GPS. Wish it worked for my love life.

questions.factBasis: Red foxes' pounces are more successful when aligned roughly NE; magnetoreception hypothesized.

questions.scene: Juniper chops an onion on your counter. Her eyes are watering. She glares at the onion.
lines: This is onion. Not feelings. Onion.
questions.question: Why does cutting onions make you cry?

choices.label: Onions are just sad vegetables
reply: Relatable. Not science.
Cutting them releases a sulfur gas that irritates your eyes.
Tip: chill the onion first. Fewer tears. Unlike breakups.

choices.label: Onions release a gas that irritates your eyes
reply: Correct. It's chemical warfare, not heartbreak.
Cutting releases a sulfur compound that turns into an eye-stinging gas.
So these tears are scientifically NOT about him. Thank you.

choices.label: You're allergic to all vegetables
reply: Then I'd only eat chips. Wait. Hm.
Onions release an eye-irritating sulfur gas when cut.
A cold onion or a sharp knife helps. Emotional tips not included.

questions.factBasis: Cutting onions releases syn-propanethial-S-oxide, a lachrymatory factor.

questions.scene: Juniper peels a banana with suspicious focus.
lines: Eating fruit. Healthy coping. My therapist would be so proud.
questions.question: Which of these is technically a berry?

choices.label: Strawberry
reply: Plot twist: strawberries aren't true berries.
Bananas are, botanically. Strawberries are a whole other thing.
Their seeds are on the outside. Trust issues, much?

choices.label: Banana
reply: Correct. Bananas are berries. Feel betrayed yet?
Botanically, bananas fit the berry definition. Strawberries don't.
Things aren't always what they're called. Like 'talking stage.'

choices.label: Raspberry
reply: Nope, betrayed by the name.
It's the banana. Botanically, bananas count as berries.
Raspberries are something else entirely. Labels lie.

questions.factBasis: Botanically, bananas are berries; strawberries and raspberries are not.

questions.scene: Juniper breaks a chocolate bar in half, eats both halves.
lines: Chocolate question. Very relevant to my current lifestyle.
questions.question: Where do cacao pods, the source of chocolate, grow?

choices.label: Directly on the trunk of the cacao tree
reply: Correct. Pods sprout straight off the trunk.
Each pod holds seeds that become chocolate after fermenting and roasting.
A tree that grows dessert on its body. Goals.

choices.label: Underground, like potatoes
reply: Underground chocolate would be a dream. No.
Cacao pods grow right off the trunk and big branches of the tree.
Imagine a tree just... sprouting chocolate pods from its body. Iconic.

choices.label: On tiny bushes in the desert
reply: Too dry. Cacao loves the tropics.
The pods grow right on the trunk and thick branches.
The beans inside become chocolate. Long process. Worth it.

questions.factBasis: Cacao is cauliflorous; pods grow directly from trunk and main branches.

questions.scene: Juniper rips open a bag of peanuts with dramatic force.
lines: Snack question. Underground edition. My two favorite things.
questions.question: Where do peanuts grow?

choices.label: On tall trees
reply: Nope. No peanut trees.
Peanuts grow underground. The flower stalk pushes into the soil.
Basically a plant that buries its own snacks. Relatable.

choices.label: Inside little pods on vines
reply: Close-ish. They are pods.
But they grow underground. The flower stalk dives into the dirt.
Peanuts are actually legumes. Like beans in disguise.

choices.label: Underground
reply: Correct. Underground snacks. My people.
The plant flowers above ground, then pushes its pods into the soil.
Peanuts are legumes, not nuts. Identity crisis. Same.

questions.factBasis: Peanuts develop underground after the flower stalk (peg) pushes into soil; they are legumes.

questions.scene: Juniper changes her phone wallpaper to a snowy mountain, then back again.
lines: I'm fine. New season, new me. Speaking of glow-ups.
questions.question: What does an Arctic fox's coat do through the year?

choices.label: Stays white all year
reply: Basic. The Arctic fox would never.
It changes color: snowy white in winter, brownish in summer.
A full seasonal rebrand. Iconic.

choices.label: Turns pink in summer
reply: Okay, I'd watch that reality show.
It switches from white in winter to brown-gray in summer.
Camouflage, not Barbiecore. Sadly.

choices.label: Changes color with the seasons
reply: Correct. The ultimate seasonal glow-up.
White in winter for snow, brownish-gray in summer to blend in.
She switches her look and nobody asks questions. Goals.

questions.factBasis: Arctic foxes molt from white winter coats to brown/gray summer coats.

questions.scene: Juniper holds up a tomato like she's in a courtroom.
lines: Is it a fruit? Is it a vegetable? Is anything what it seems? Anyway.
questions.question: In 1893, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that tomatoes were legally what?

choices.label: A fruit
reply: Botanically, yes. Legally? Plot twist.
The court ruled tomatoes a vegetable, for tax reasons.
Science said fruit. The law said vegetable. Complicated relationship.

choices.label: A vegetable
reply: Correct. Legally a vegetable.
Botanically it's a fruit, but the court went with how people cook it.
Labels are complicated. I'm 'single' but also 'it's complicated.'

choices.label: A berry
reply: Botanically it IS a berry. The law didn't care.
The court called it a vegetable, mostly about import taxes.
Two identities. Relatable tomato.

questions.factBasis: Nix v. Hedden (1893) classified tomatoes as vegetables for tariff purposes.

questions.scene: Juniper drizzles honey on toast and doesn't make eye contact.
lines: I'm fine. This one's about something that lasts. Unlike some people.
questions.question: What's special about honey?

choices.label: It can basically never spoil
reply: Yep. Honey is forever. Unlike some boyfriends.
Edible honey has been found in ancient Egyptian tombs.
Low water, high sugar, no germs. Main character food.

choices.label: It's made from bee tears
reply: Bees cry? Okay, now I'm sad.
No, it's nectar. And properly stored, honey basically never spoils.
Archaeologists found edible honey in ancient tombs.

choices.label: It glows in the dark
reply: That would be iconic for midnight toast.
Real fact: stored right, honey basically never spoils.
Edible honey turned up in ancient Egyptian tombs.

questions.factBasis: Properly stored honey is extremely resistant to spoiling; edible honey reported in ancient Egyptian tombs.

questions.scene: Juniper puts a hand on her chest, then quickly pretends she's adjusting her scarf.
lines: Heart question. Medical. Not personal. Completely unrelated to anything.
questions.question: Can intense emotional stress actually affect your heart?

choices.label: No, that's just a metaphor
reply: Turns out it's more than a metaphor.
'Broken heart syndrome' is a real, usually temporary heart condition from intense stress.
Most people recover fully. Note to self. I mean, note to everyone.

choices.label: Yes, there's a real condition called 'broken heart syndrome'
reply: Yes. It's real. Doctors call it takotsubo.
Sudden intense stress can temporarily weaken the heart muscle.
Usually it recovers. Which is good news. For everyone. Hypothetically.

choices.label: Only in movies
reply: Movies got this one right, weirdly.
Broken heart syndrome is real and triggered by intense stress.
It usually heals. Hearts are tougher than they look.

questions.factBasis: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy ('broken heart syndrome') is a usually reversible stress-induced heart condition.

questions.scene: Juniper scrolls through photos of pink birds standing on one leg.
lines: They're so dramatic. I love them. Unrelated: I'm also dramatic.
questions.question: Why are flamingos pink?

choices.label: From pigments in the food they eat
reply: Correct. Diet-based glow-up.
Pigments called carotenoids in algae and shrimp tint their feathers pink.
No pink snacks, no pink bird. Respect the commitment.

choices.label: They're born pink and stay that way
reply: Nope. Baby flamingos are gray-white.
They turn pink from pigments in the algae and shrimp they eat.
You are what you eat. I'm currently 40% chips.

choices.label: Sunburn from standing in the sun all day
reply: Ouch. No.
Their pink comes from pigments in their algae and shrimp diet.
Chicks start gray. The pink is earned.

questions.factBasis: Flamingo coloration comes from dietary carotenoids.

questions.scene: Juniper opens your fridge without asking and stands there thinking.
lines: Don't mind me. Doing research. On comfort food. For science.
questions.question: Bad day comfort food: sweet or salty?

choices.label: Sweet
reply: Sweet. Ice cream therapy.
Free, cold, and never cancels plans.

choices.label: Salty
reply: Salty. Chips first, questions later.
Crunch is emotional support.

A:A: You both go sweet. A two-spoon household.
Get a pint for you and a pint for {partner}. No sharing drama.
I'm fine. I just want ice cream now.
A:B: Salty for you, sweet for {partner}.
Honestly ideal. Zero snack competition.
Fries dipped in a milkshake. Try it. Life-changing.
B:A: Sweet for you, salty for {partner}.
Perfect. Nobody steals anybody's snack.
Chocolate-covered pretzels. Peace treaty.
B:B: Salty for both of you. Crunch squad.
So you and {partner} probably fight over the last chip.
Buy two bags. Love is logistics.

questions.scene: Juniper glances at your phone lock screen, then pretends she didn't.
lines: I'm fine. Totally not looking. Okay I looked.
questions.question: Your phone wallpaper: a photo of you two, or literally anything else?

choices.label: A photo of us
reply: A couple photo? Cute. Disgusting. Cute.
Your lock screen is a soft launch.

choices.label: Anything else
reply: Anything else? Mysterious.
A sunset, a cat, a meme. Respect.

A:A: Both of you use a couple photo. Okay, adorable.
Honestly, you and {partner} are a hard launch couple.
I'm fine. My wallpaper is a croissant.
A:B: You keep it random. {partner} uses a photo of you two.
They're down bad, in a sweet way.
Maybe match them. Just for a week. See what happens.
B:A: Couple photo for you. {partner} keeps it mysterious.
Their lock screen might be a sandwich. Don't take it personally.
Send them your favorite pic. Just as a suggestion.
B:B: Neither of you uses a couple photo. Low-key love.
I can picture it: you and {partner} keep it private. Mature.
Croissant wallpaper gang. Welcome.

questions.scene: Juniper steals a fry from your plate and looks you dead in the eye.
lines: This fry looked lonely. I rescued it.
questions.question: Food-sharing rule?

choices.label: Order two, share both
reply: Share both. Diplomatic.
Two dishes, double the joy.

choices.label: Hands off my plate
reply: Hands off. A boundary. Healthy.
Some fries are not for sharing.

choices.label: Say 'not hungry,' then eat theirs
reply: Ah, the classic fry thief.
Not hungry, but hungry for theirs.

A:A: Order two and share. You and {partner} are a buffet couple.
Every dinner is a tasting menu with a side of forks crossing.
Rowan never shared his fries. Not that I think about it. Next.
A:B: Hands off your plate. {partner} wants to share.
They'll keep offering bites. You'll keep saying no.
Give them one fry. Just one. It's love.
A:C: You steal food. {partner} likes sharing. Easy.
They're basically an open buffet for you.
B:A: You share both dishes. {partner} guards their plate.
Rough. Your fork will get rejected.
Ask first. Or order extra fries for the middle.
B:B: Hands off for both of you. Respect.
Pretty sure you and {partner} each guard your plates like treasure.
No tension. Separate fries, happy hearts.
B:C: {partner} will catch you. They always do.
Ask nicely. Or bribe them with dessert.
C:A: You love sharing. {partner} pretends they're not hungry.
Then eats half your plate while saying 'I'm good.'
Order an extra side just for them. Label it 'not hungry fries.'
C:B: Hands off your plate. {partner} is a fry thief.
Oof. You'll need a fork shield.
Or order one extra fries just for them.
C:C: You're both fry thieves. Absolute chaos.
Lowkey, you and {partner} will reach for the same fry at the same time.
Order extra fries for the middle. Or fight. Your call.

questions.scene: Juniper grabs your remote and scrolls past every rom-com, very fast.
lines: Nope. Skip. Skip. Not that one. Okay, movie question.
questions.question: Movie night: rom-com, or something with explosions?

choices.label: Rom-com
reply: Rom-com. Brave choice around me.
I won't cry. Okay, I might.

choices.label: Explosions
reply: Explosions. Loud. Safe. Emotionally.
No kissing scenes. Just cars flipping.

A:A: Both rom-com. Tissues on standby.
You and {partner} probably mouth the lines together.
I'm fine. I'm not crying. You're crying.
A:B: Explosions for you. {partner} wants a rom-com.
Watch theirs first. Hold their hand at the sad part.
Then blow stuff up. Balance.
B:A: Rom-com for you. {partner} wants explosions.
Plot twist: some rom-coms have car chases.
Or alternate nights. Fair is fair.
B:B: Both explosions. Volume up.
So you and {partner} prefer feelings in the form of car chases.
Popcorn plus fire. Iconic.

questions.scene: Juniper unlocks her phone, then deletes a photo with zero hesitation.
lines: That photo didn't exist. You saw nothing.
questions.question: Phone passwords: share everything, or some things stay private?

choices.label: Share everything
reply: Open phone policy. Bold.
Nothing to hide but your search history.

choices.label: Some things stay private
reply: Privacy. Healthy and valid.
Trust doesn't need passwords.

A:A: Full password sharing for both of you. Trust era.
Honestly, you and {partner} could swap phones and survive.
I'm fine. I'd delete my notes app first.
A:B: You like privacy. {partner} shares everything.
Tell them it's not about secrets. It's about you.
Then maybe share one thing. Like your favorite meme folder.
B:A: You'd share everything. {partner} likes some privacy.
That's okay. Trust isn't a password.
Give them space. They'll share when they're ready.
B:B: You both keep some things private. Respect.
Trust without passwords. You and {partner} are mature.
Very healthy. Juniper approves.

questions.scene: Juniper opens three snack bags at once, side by side.
lines: Before you ask, this is a normal amount of snacks.
questions.question: On a bad day, what's your partner's go-to snack?
questions.selfQuestion: On a bad day, what's your go-to snack?

choices.label: Ice cream
reply: Ice cream. Classic heartbreak food.
I'm fine. I'm not eating ice cream. Shut up.

choices.label: Chips
reply: Chips. Crunch therapy.
Can't cry when you're crunching.

choices.label: Midnight instant noodles
reply: Midnight noodles. Unhinged. Respect.
Comfort in a cup at 2 a.m.

A:A: Ice cream, and {partner} called it.
They've seen you with a spoon and a sad face before.
Keep a pint in the freezer. Emergency use only.
A:B: Chips for you. {partner} guessed ice cream.
They're showing up with a pint while you want crunch.
Tell them. Or take both.
A:C: Midnight noodles for you. {partner} guessed ice cream.
Cold vs hot. Opposite ends of the freezer.
Time to tell them your 2 a.m. secret.
B:A: Ice cream for you. {partner} guessed chips.
They've been bringing the wrong snack. Gently correct them.
Or do sweet and salty together. Peak bad-day combo.
B:B: Chips, and {partner} called it.
They know the crunch means you're struggling.
Hide a bag somewhere. For emergencies.
B:C: Midnight noodles for you. {partner} guessed chips.
They show up with a bag while you're boiling water.
Tell them your 2 a.m. kettle is a cry for help.
C:A: Ice cream for you. {partner} guessed midnight noodles.
Ice cream at midnight still counts.
C:B: Chips for you. {partner} guessed midnight noodles.
Crush chips on top of noodles. Trust me. Life-changing.
C:C: They've heard the kettle at 2 a.m. They know.

questions.scene: Juniper smiles a little too wide.
lines: I'm fine. Totally fine. Why do you ask?
questions.question: When your partner says 'I'm fine,' what does it actually mean?
questions.selfQuestion: When you say 'I'm fine,' what does it actually mean?

choices.label: Actually fine
reply: Actually fine? Rare. Lucky you.
Some people mean it. Not me, but some people.

choices.label: Absolutely not fine
reply: Not fine. Classic.
The 'I'm fine' that hits like thunder.

A:A: Actually fine, and {partner} trusts it.
When you say it, you mean it. Good communication.
I'm fine. Okay, I'm jealous.
A:B: You're not fine. {partner} thought you meant it.
Oof. Time for a new code word.
Try 'I'm fine-ish.' That's a cry for snacks.
B:A: You're actually fine. {partner} thinks you're secretly not.
They'll keep checking on you. Kind of cute.
Say 'really fine' with a smile. Then they'll relax.
B:B: Not fine, and {partner} knows it.
They can tell the 'I'm fine' that means 'please hug me.'
Real ones know. Keep them close.

questions.scene: Juniper casually checks someone's social media, then closes it fast.
lines: Not jealous. Just checking. Who even posts that much? Anyway.
questions.question: How does your partner act when they're a little jealous?
questions.selfQuestion: How do you act when you're a little jealous?

choices.label: Goes quiet
reply: Quiet jealous. Silent but deadly.
One sigh. Seven meanings. All of them about that one coworker.

choices.label: Makes a joke about it
reply: Joke jealous. Hides it in a meme.
'Haha who's THAT' is never just a joke.

A:A: You go quiet, and {partner} knew.
They've learned your silence has a volume. A loud one.
Say one honest sentence next time. Saves you both an hour.
A:B: You joke about it. {partner} expected silence.
They'll laugh at the joke and completely miss the feeling under it.
Say it once, straight. Then go back to joking. Balance.
B:A: You go quiet. {partner} expected a joke.
So they're waiting for a meme while you're doing a full silent movie.
Try one tiny joke, then one tiny truth. Works on foxes.
B:B: You joke about it, and {partner} knew.
They can hear the jealousy hiding inside your 'lol.'
Funny is fine. Add one real line after. I'm working on that too.

questions.scene: Juniper hums a breakup ballad, then switches to a pop song fast.
lines: I wasn't singing about him. Songs are songs.
questions.question: What's your partner's karaoke energy?

choices.label: Main character, full choreography
reply: Full choreography. Star behavior.
Grabs the mic and doesn't let go.

choices.label: Hides behind the snack menu
reply: Snack menu hider. Shy legend.
Present, supportive, eating fries.

A:A: Main character, and {partner} knew it.
They've seen your shower concerts. They've been warned.
Next time, duet. Make it a moment.
A:B: You hide behind the menu. {partner} expected a performance.
Sorry, they're waiting for a show you won't give.
Tell them you'll clap. Loudly. That's your role.
B:A: You're a karaoke star. {partner} thought you'd hide.
Surprise! Drag them up for a duet.
Watching them see your full choreography? Priceless.
B:B: Snack menu hider, and {partner} knew.
They know you'd rather eat fries than sing.
Fair. Someone has to hold the snacks.

questions.scene: Juniper pulls out an old ticket stub and stares at it, then puts it away quickly.
lines: First dates. I'm fine. Don't ask why I'm fine.
questions.question: How would your partner describe your first date?
questions.selfQuestion: How would you describe your first date?

choices.label: Magical
reply: Magical. Okay, movie scene.
Sparkles, slow motion, everything.

choices.label: Chaotic
reply: Chaotic. The best kind of story.
Something went wrong, and it was perfect.

choices.label: Awkward but cute
reply: Awkward but cute. The realest kind.
Weird pauses, cute smiles.

A:A: Magical for both of you. Disgusting. Cute.
{partner} remembers the sparkle too. Same movie, same soundtrack.
I'm fine. Not crying. It's allergies. To happiness.
A:B: Chaos for you. {partner} remembers magic.
They saw sparkles through all the chaos.
That's love goggles. Keep them.
A:C: Awkward but cute for you. {partner} remembers pure magic.
They completely missed the weird pauses. Lucky you.
Never tell them. Let them keep the movie version.
B:A: Magical for you. {partner} remembers chaos.
Same date, different movie genres.
Rewatch it together. Who's right?
B:B: Chaotic, and {partner} agrees.
Spilled drinks? Wrong restaurant? Rain? That's the lore.
Retell it every anniversary. Add one fake detail each year.
B:C: Awkward but cute for you. {partner} remembers chaos.
You remember the pauses. They remember the disasters.
Either way, look at you two now. Rude. Cute.
C:A: Magical for you. {partner} remembers awkward but cute.
They were sweating through the whole thing. You saw fireworks.
Tell them their nerves were invisible. Even if they weren't.
C:B: Chaos for you. {partner} remembers awkward but cute.
So something went wrong AND nobody knew what to say?
And you still came back for date two. That's love.
C:C: Weird pauses, nervous laughs, and somehow, a second date.
That's the realest kind. Movies lie. Awkward is honest.
